title: 1 Music Grade 5 Lesson Plans
text:
SCHOOL LEARNING AREA GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 MUSIC 5
STRAND: PERFORMING
SUB STRAND: Sing songs to express different moods- patriotic songs
SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: by the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
1. Sing different types of songs with expressions
2. State reason why people sing patriotic songs
3. Appreciate the different types of songs
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (S)
Why do people express themselves as they sing?
LEARNING RESOURCES
Foundation music grade 5 page 1-4, digital devices
ORGANISATION OF LEARNING
Learning will take place in an actual classroom. Learners will work individually, in pairs and
small groups.
INTRODUCTION
Guide the pupils to listen and watch recorded performance.
  Digital literacy: developed through manipulation and use of digital devices to learn songs
LESSON DEVELOPMENT
STEP 1
In groups pupils to discuss the words in the song they have just listened and also discuss
how to express the mood portrayed by the words in the songs.
  The core competency of communication and collaboration will be developed as the
 learner discuss.
STEP 2
In group’s learners to practise singing a patriotic song. ‘’Kenya taifa letu’’ .
  Patriotism is instilled alongside other values through singing patriotic songs, with messages
 on love, respect, unity and peace.
STEP 3
Teacher to guide the learners in singing patriotic songs ensuring they sing patriotic songs
ensuring they sing the tune and rhythm correctly and apply the correct dynamics.
CONCLUSION:
Discuss the message found in the patriotic song.
  Respect: instilled during peer review sessions as learners learn to respect each other’s views.
Sing for enjoyment
EXTENDED ACTIVITIES:
Perform a patriotic song during social events
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON:

 MUSIC 5
STRAND: PERFORMING
SUB STRAND: Singing song with expressions to show mood- sacred, topical and popular
songs
SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: by the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
1. Sing different types of songs with expressions
2. State reason why people sing topical songs
3. Appreciate the different types of songs
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (S)
Why do people express themselves as they sing?
LEARNING RESOURCES
Foundation music grade 4-5page, digital devices
ORGANISATION OF LEARNING
Learning will take place in an actual classroom. Learners will work individually, in pairs and
small groups.
INTRODUCTION
Teacher to review the previous lesson
Guide the pupils to listen and watch recorded performance.
  Digital literacy: developed through manipulation and use of digital devices to learn songs
LESSON DEVELOPMENT
STEP 1
In groups pupils to discuss the words in the song they have just listened and also discuss
how to express the mood portrayed by the words in the songs.
  Communication and Collaboration: developed through interpretation of the meaning of a song
 and presentation of the same to convey the appropriate mood
STEP 2
In group’s learners to practise singing a topical song.
‘’wash your hands’’
STEP 3
Teacher to guide the learners in singing topical song ensuring the tune and rhythm are

CONCLUSION:
Discuss the message found in the topical song.
Sing for enjoyment
  Learners discuss the words of topical issues addressing different PCI’s and get to learn more

EXTENDED ACTIVITIES:
Perform topical songs during community events.
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON:

 MUSIC 5
STRAND: PERFORMING
SUB STRAND: Sing the East African Community Anthem
SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: by the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
1. Sing the EAC anthem
2. State the meaning singing in unison
3. Appreciate the different types of songs
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (S)
Why is the East African Community Anthem important?
LEARNING RESOURCES
Foundation music grade 5 page 7-9, digital devices
ORGANISATION OF LEARNING
Learning will take place in an actual classroom. Learners will work individually, in pairs and
small groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson
Learners’ to sing Kenya National Anthem.
  Citizenship: discussing the words and singing the anthem enhances citizenship.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT
STEP 1
Guide the pupils to listen and watch recorded performance of EACA
  Digital literacy: developed through manipulation and use of digital devices to learn songs
STEP 2
Learners to practise singing EACA in Kiswahili with accuracy in tune proper dictation and
articulation of words
  Patriotism is instilled alongside other values through singing EACA, with messages on love,
 respect, unity and peace.
STEP 3
In groups learners to discuss the meaning of the words of the EACA and the values learnt
from the anthem
  Respect: instilled during peer review sessions as learners learn to respect each other’s views
CONCLUSION:
Discuss the message found in the EACA song.
Sing for enjoyment
EXTENDED ACTIVITIES:
Perform EACA during social events
Practise singing EACA in English
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON:

 MUSIC 5
STRAND: PERFORMING
SUB STRAND: Sing a three-part song
SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: by the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
1. Define the term part singing
2. Sing in a 3 part song for perception of harmony and enjoyment
3. Appreciate the different types of songs
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (S)
Why is part singing?
LEARNING RESOURCES
Foundation music grade 5 page 9, Digital devices
ORGANISATION OF LEARNING
Learning will take place in an actual classroom. Learners will work individually, in pairs and
small groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson
Engage the learners to watch live/recorded performance of a three part musical
performance
  Digital literacy: developed through manipulation and use of digital devices to learn songs
LESSON DEVELOPMENT
STEP 1
Teacher to involve learners in discussing the performance observed/listened to using the
key inquiry question.
STEP 2
Teacher to divide the learners into three groups and assign each group a part to sing (one
group sing the main melody while the other group sings the second part)
  Communication and Collaboration: Enhanced also through singing in groups (choral/three-
 part songs) and group discussion.
STEP 3
In groups learners to sing their part simultaneously as guide by the teacher
  Learning to learn: enhanced in use of knowledge acquired in performance of different types
 of songs to learn and perform a three part song.
CONCLUSION:
Engage the learners in observing accuracy in pitch and rhythm and using dynamics as they
sing three part song.
Sing for enjoyment
EXTENDED ACTIVITIES:
Practise to sing the song music alone shall live
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON:

 MUSIC 5
STRAND: PERFORMING
SUB STRAND: appreciating the use of expressions in singing
SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: by the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
1. Sing different types of songs with expressions
2. State reason why people sing different types of songs
3. Appreciate the different types of songs
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (S)
Why do people express themselves as they sing?
LEARNING RESOURCES
Foundation music grade 10-11 page, digital devices
ORGANISATION OF LEARNING
Learning will take place in an actual classroom. Learners will work individually, in pairs and
small groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
Guide the pupils to listen and watch recorded performance.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT
STEP 1
In groups pupils to discuss the type of song, expressions and message passed from the
different sons they have just watched.
Learners also to listened and discuss how to express the mood portrayed by the words in
the songs.
  The core competency of communication and collaboration will be developed as the
 learner discuss.
STEP 2
Learners to choose two types of songs
In groups learners to practise different types of song.
  Creativity and imagination is developed through application of appropriate
 expressions during singing
STEP 3
Teacher to guide the learners to present the songs in class as other learns listen.
 Ensuring they sing the tune and rhythm correctly and apply the correct dynamics.
  Critical thinking and problem solving: enhanced during peer review sessions where they do
 critique peers’ presentations citing areas of improvement
CONCLUSION:
Record the song using digital devices for use in class.
Sing for enjoyment
  Digital literacy: developed through manipulation and use of digital devices to learn songs
EXTENDED ACTIVITIES:
Perform a song during school functions and social events
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON:

 MUSIC 5
STRAND: PERFORMING
SUB STRAND: aspect of folk songs – participants and instruments
SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: by the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
1. Discuss aspect of a folk song
2. State the instruments used in a folk song
3. Appreciate role of folk songs drawn from diverse communities in Kenya.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (S)
Why is it important to learn folk song from different community?
Which instruments are used to accompany the folk songs?
LEARNING RESOURCES
Foundation music grade 5 page 14-15, digital devices, Drum
ORGANISATION OF LEARNING
Learning will take place in an actual classroom. Learners will work individually, in pairs and
small groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson
Engage the learners to watch live/recorded performance of a folk song
  Digital literacy: developed through manipulation and use of digital devices to learn songs
LESSON DEVELOPMENT
STEP 1
Using the key inquiry question guide the learners in identifying participants and instruments
used in the folk songs
  Critical thinking: listening and discussing different aspects (participants and instruments)
 of folk songs enhances critical thinking and problem solving
STEP 2
Guide the learners in discussing the roles of participants and instruments in a folk song
performance
  Communication and Collaboration: is developed as learners discuss the aspects of folk songs
 in groups and holding group discussions
STEP 3
Divide the learners into groups, assign each group instruments and involved them in singing
a familiar folk song
  Value of Responsibility is instilled by learners taking different roles in folk songs
Guide the learners to sing folk song while accompanying them with appropriate musical
instrument
CONCLUSION:
Encourage the learners to explore their skills on the instrument
Sing for enjoyment
EXTENDED ACTIVITIES:
Perform a folk song during social events, Watch a Maasai folk song
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON:

CONCLUSION:

 MUSIC 5
STRAND: PERFORMING
SUB STRAND: performing folk songs from diverse culture
SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: by the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
1. Discuss aspect of a folk song
2. State the instruments used in a folk song
3. Appreciate role of folk songs drawn from diverse communities in Kenya.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (S)
Why is it important to learn folk song from different community?
Which instruments are used to accompany the folk songs
What makes a folk song?
LEARNING RESOURCES
Foundation music grade 5 page 15-17, digital devices
ORGANISATION OF LEARNING
Learning will take place in an actual classroom. Learners will work individually, in pairs and
small groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson
Engage the learners to watch live/recorded performance of a folk song
  Digital literacy: developed through manipulation and use of digital devices to watch a folk
 song.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT
STEP 1
Guide the learners in identifying a folk song from a community in Kenya.
  Citizenship: developed through identifying folk songs from diverse communities in
 Kenya
STEP 2
Guide the learners in discussing the different roles played by the participants in the folk
song performance
  Value of Patriotism and Respect-acquired through performing folk songs from diverse
 Kenyan communities
STEP 3
Divide the learners into groups, assign each group instruments and involved them in singing
and performing a familiar folk song
Guide the learners to perform the folk song taking into consideration the different roles of
the participants while accompanying them with appropriate musical instrument
  Value of Unity-Team work in performance of folk songs facilitates unity
CONCLUSION:
Perform the folk song before the class as classmate watch and give their views
  Self-efficacy: developed through taking different roles in the performance of folk songs.
Sing for enjoyment
EXTENDED ACTIVITIES:
Perform a folk song during social events
Watch a Luo folk song

 MUSIC 5
STRAND: PERFORMING
SUB STRAND: coordinated movements when performing a folk song
SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES: by the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
1. Sing folk songs drawn from local communities
2. Perform folk song with coordinated body movement
3. Appreciate role of folk songs drawn from diverse communities in Kenya.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (S)
What is the message in the folk song?
Why is it important to learn folk songs from different communities in Kenya?
What makes a folk song?
LEARNING RESOURCES
Foundation music grade 5 page 17-19, digital devices, drums, props
ORGANISATION OF LEARNING
Learning will take place in an actual classroom. Learners will work individually, in pairs and
small groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson
Engage the learners to watch live/recorded performance of a folk song
  Digital literacy: developed through manipulation and use of digital devices to learn songs.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT
STEP 1
Guide the learners in identifying the body movements of folk song watched, learners to
observe appropriate behaviour from the recorded performance
  Learning to learn: enhanced in use of knowledge acquired in performance of different types
 of folk songs to identify the coordinated movements
STEP 2
Lead learners in imitating the movements observed from recorded performance and
photographs/picture of folk song performance observed earlier in the learner’s book
  Core Competencies to be developed-Safety- enhanced through observing safety in
 performance of a folk song.
STEP 3
Divide the learners into groups; assign each group a particular song
Involve learners in performing the folk song with appropriate coordinated body movements
  Citizenship: developed through performing folk songs from diverse communities in
 Kenya
CONCLUSION:
In groups guide learners to perform folk songs while accompanying them with appropriate
musical instruments
In group’s learners to perform folk song while capturing the appropriate mood, observing
good manners while making coordinated body movements
  Self-efficacy: developed through taking different roles in the performance of folk songs.
Sing for enjoyment
EXTENDED ACTIVITIES:
Perform a folk song during social events, Watch a kisii folk song
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON:
